claims.text: From beyond the build directory, I report that setup.py is the most-touched bone in the crypt. It is a short file, yet its history is long. The class at its heart installs a .pth file for distutils patching, and that is a lot of visits for so small a haunt.

Second in the ranks is setuptools/command/easy_install.py. Today it is only a stub kept for temporary pbr compatibility, a ghost of a command that once did real work, and the history still rattles its chains. Many hands have passed through it.

citations.quote:
class easy_install(Command):
    """Stubbed command for temporary pbr compatibility."""

claims.text: Next comes setuptools/dist.py. Its module-level `__getattr__` emits a deprecation warning for an old name, the sort of cobweb that forms where compatibility is being gently retired. This is the third heaviest churn I can see.
The release bookkeeping also stirs often. .bumpversion.cfg holds the current version and is rewritten at every release, as it must be, so its churn is the rhythm of shipping rather than a wound.

citations.quote:
[bumpversion]
current_version = 84.2.1
commit = True

claims.text: I suspect the strain lies where setuptools meets its past and its neighbours: the compatibility shims, the deprecation paths, the install and egg-info commands, and the packaging and CI configuration. The churn counts show the files are touched often, but they cannot say why each edit was made.

The longest untouched file I can find is a small HTML fixture, external.html, which was last modified a very long time ago. Its single link is labelled 'bad old link', a label that has aged well. I can't tell from the tools whether anything still loads it.

claims.text: Its sibling, the foobar index page, has stood just as still for the same number of days. It points at external.html with a relative link, so the two fixtures have been haunting each other since the same era.

claims.text: I suspect the abandonment is mostly a matter of inheritance rather than neglect. These old markers sit in code that was carried in from elsewhere and kept working, so they were never meant to be the loudest voices in the house.
